name: Reptilia
note: Root of the tree: living reptile groups plus the extinct relatives shown here.

name: Mesosauria
note: Early Permian aquatic reptiles. Placement is debated: either the earliest-branching reptiles or early parareptiles. Their anapsid skull (no openings behind the eye) is the ancestral condition, not a sign of kinship with turtles.

name: Sauria
note: Last common ancestor of lepidosaurs and archelosaurs.

name: Archelosauria
note: Turtles are the closest living relatives of archosaurs (crocodiles and birds).
citation: Crawford et al. 2015, Mol Phylogenet Evol 83:250-257

name: Testudines
note: The turtle skull lacks openings behind the eye, but this is secondary: stem turtles descend from diapsid ancestors.

name: Archosauria
citation: Nesbitt 2011, Bull Am Mus Nat Hist 352:1-292

name: Crocodylia
note: The only living members of the crocodile line (Pseudosuchia); extinct pseudosuchians are not shown.
citation: Nesbitt 2011, Bull Am Mus Nat Hist 352:1-292

name: Pterosauria
note: Flying reptiles; the closest relatives of dinosaurs. Extinct at the end of the Cretaceous.

name: Ornithischia
note: Beaked, mostly plant-eating dinosaurs. The minority Ornithoscelida hypothesis (Baron et al. 2017) groups them with theropods instead; the traditional split is shown.

name: Saurischia
note: Sauropodomorphs plus theropods, which include birds.

name: Sauropodomorpha
note: Long-necked dinosaurs. Shown so that Saurischia has a real split.

name: Aves
note: Birds are living theropod dinosaurs; non-avian theropods are not shown.
